site_article.headline: Anthropic launches Claude Sheets, Meetings and Whiteboards as Microsoft shares slip
site_article.dek: The new beta tools put a spreadsheet, a meeting agent and a shared whiteboard inside Claude, days before the company's planned IPO.
site_article.summary: Anthropic introduced Claude Sheets, Claude Meetings and Claude Whiteboards on November 10, 2026, and renamed Claude Dashboards to Claude Data. Microsoft shares fell about 2% after the news.
site_article.seo_title: Anthropic launches Claude Sheets, Meetings and Whiteboards
site_article.seo_description: Anthropic added a spreadsheet, a video call agent, shared whiteboards and Claude Data to Claude. Microsoft stock fell about 2% on the news.
site_article.answer_summary: Claude Sheets is a beta spreadsheet built into Claude for paid plans. Anthropic launched it on November 10, 2026, together with Claude Meetings, Claude Whiteboards and Claude Data.
site_article.hero_alt: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella with a serious expression.

paragraphs.text: Anthropic introduced a set of workplace tools on November 10, 2026, including Claude Sheets, Claude Meetings and Claude Whiteboards, according to TechCrunch and Engadget. The company also renamed its Claude Dashboards product to Claude Data and expanded how outside apps can run inside Claude.

Microsoft shares fell about 2% on Tuesday after reports of the launch, Yahoo Finance and Investing.com reported. Investing.com said the move followed a Bloomberg report that Anthropic planned a spreadsheet app that competes with Microsoft Excel and Google Sheets.

Claude Sheets is a spreadsheet built into Claude in which a user and Claude edit the same cells. According to Anthropic's help center, Claude can create tabs, write formulas, apply formatting and conditional formatting, and add dropdowns, checkboxes and charts. Formulas stay visible in the cells, and sheets are saved in the Artifacts tab.

The help center lists the product as a beta for Pro, Max, Ultra, Team and Enterprise plans. It is on by default for Team plans, while Enterprise administrators must switch it on. Each sheet can hold up to 100,000 cells. Users can import CSV, Excel or Google Sheets files and export to .xlsx or CSV.

Anthropic also lists clear gaps. Pivot tables, find and replace, filter views and PDF export are not yet available, and macros, VBA and Power Query are not supported. Engadget reported that several people with edit access can work on one file and that Claude's changes are logged so coworkers can follow them.

According to Investing.com, Anthropic product leader Nicholas Lin told Bloomberg that Claude Sheets is still a basic product that is not designed for sophisticated financial modeling, and that the company expects its integrations with existing spreadsheet software to remain better for those tasks.

Claude Meetings adds Claude to a video call as a visible participant. TechCrunch reported that during a call it can draft the plan being discussed, map a timeline on a whiteboard, answer questions in the meeting chat and pull information from connected work apps. Notes and action items are available in claude.ai afterward.

Meetings is in beta for Team and Enterprise plans and works only with Google Meet at launch. Claude posts a notice in the chat, will not join calls with outside guests unless an administrator allows it, and leaves if an outside guest joins, according to TechCrunch and Engadget.

Claude Whiteboards, also in beta for paid plans, turns a team's planning discussion into a shared board with timelines and deadlines, and a finished board can be converted into a document or slide deck, TechCrunch reported. Claude Data connects to systems such as a data warehouse or CRM and answers questions with dashboards, written data stories or narrated videos.

Engadget reported that Anthropic is also letting users open full versions of partner apps inside Claude, starting with Adobe, Atlassian and HubSpot, and that Claude already offers more than 9,000 connectors.

The launch comes as Anthropic begins the roadshow for its initial public offering, which Yahoo Finance said is expected on November 19 or November 20. Investing.com noted that Microsoft is among the companies taking part in a separate $26 billion private placement tied to the offering.

The products move Anthropic from offering an assistant that works alongside other companies' software toward offering its own versions of everyday office apps. The company's own description of Sheets as basic suggests the near term goal is quick team tasks such as trackers and budgets rather than replacing heavy Excel work, but the market reaction shows investors are watching any overlap with Microsoft 365 closely.

Watch whether Claude Meetings expands beyond Google Meet to Zoom or Microsoft Teams, and how quickly Sheets fills gaps such as pivot tables, since those steps would bring it closer to competing with Excel directly.
